ce2_special_check.finding: Evidence identical, Judgment different, Requirement SAME
ce2_special_check.implication: Handoff Pattern valid: same boundary → same requirement. Difference in judgment from semantic content, not evidence need. DICE can prepare same Evidence Package for both; Human makes different judgments using same evidence.
ce2_special_check.requirement_vs_answer: Pattern predicts REQUIREMENT (what evidence to prepare), not ANSWER (what judgment to make)

evidence_learning_path.allowed: Human Judgment → Evidence Requirement → Boundary Handoff Pattern Candidate → Future Human Handoff
safety_conditions: Record WHAT evidence was needed, NOT what answer was given
Requirement is about EVIDENCE TYPE, not SEMANTIC LABEL
Pattern does NOT predict judgment (CE2 proves same pattern, different judgment)
Pattern is CANDIDATE, not validated signal

unlearnable_boundary_check.result: ALL 18 cases fit into a pattern. No case is completely unlearnable in terms of Evidence Requirement.

answer_vs_requirement.answer: Cannot be learned from structural evidence (CE2 proves: identical evidence → different judgment; R5=100%, R6=100%)
answer_vs_requirement.requirement: CAN be learned from boundary type (4 stable patterns across 18 cases; CE2 proves: same boundary → same requirement)
answer_vs_requirement.principle: DICE does NOT learn 'this text is a caption.' DICE DOES learn 'caption-vs-reference boundaries need local context + semantic understanding.'
answer_vs_requirement.relationship: DICE = Evidence Provider (prepares what Human needs); Human = Semantic Judge (makes irreducible judgment); G5 = boundary between them

limitations.limitation: SINGLE HUMAN REVIEWER — requirements may be reviewer-specific
NO IMPLEMENTATION TEST — B3 level is theoretical
P3 NOT CROSS-DOCUMENT — AUTHOR_NAME_RECOGNITION has only 1 doc
R5=100% means NO structural expansion can eliminate semantic need
PATTERN ≠ SIGNAL — candidates, not validated signals
CE2 IS SINGLE INSTANCE — more pairs would strengthen finding
NO HUMAN TIME DATA — cannot claim review time decreases

final_questions.Q2_cross_case_repeat: YES — 4 patterns with repeated requirements across 18 cases
final_questions.Q3_cross_document: YES — 3/4 patterns are cross-document (16/18 = 88.9% of cases)
final_questions.Q4_ce2_requirement_same: YES — Evidence identical, Judgment different, Requirement SAME. Pattern valid.
final_questions.Q5_stable_boundary_requirement: YES — 3 REUSABLE + 1 CONDITIONAL patterns. Same boundary → same requirement.
final_questions.Q6_handoff_pattern: YES — 4 Pattern Candidates (3 REUSABLE, 1 CONDITIONAL). All at B2.
final_questions.Q8_no_stable_pattern: 0/18 (0%) — all cases fit into a pattern. Judgment unlearnable but requirement learnable.
final_questions.Q9_safe_conversion: YES — with strict conditions. Record requirement, not answer. CE2 proves no answer leakage.
final_questions.Q10_next_step: STOP — all patterns at B2; B3 requires implementation (not authorized); no further READ-ONLY research possible
